title: Disagree Constructively and Move the Discussion Forward
status: New proposed full-lesson production plan, not a recovered previously approved Lesson04 outline.
continuity: Lesson01 introduced a shared discussion; Lesson02 developed reasons and their limits; Lesson03 deepened listening and connected responses. Lesson04 applies those resources to disagreement, comparing alternatives and keeping the decision state accurate.
boundaries: Seven sections fit these learning steps; seven is not mandatory for all future lessons.
This lesson addresses ordinary constructive disagreement, not formal negotiation, conflict mediation or methods for winning an argument.
No compulsory acknowledgement formula, manufactured agreement, automatic compromise or claimed consensus.
Original fictional examples are not real exam questions, official criteria or observed outcomes.
English silent review only; final recorded audio and localization are handled in the downstream production pass.

sections.title: Locate the Point of Disagreement
sections.learningOutcome: Identify the specific proposal, reason or unresolved detail being challenged; disagree with a claim without inventing a motive or rejecting every related idea.

sections.title: Recognise a Reason Without Pretending to Agree
sections.learningOutcome: Acknowledge a genuinely relevant reason while stating a real reservation; distinguish recognition from agreement and avoid using personal judgements as objections.

sections.title: Explain the Concern Precisely
sections.learningOutcome: State a task-related concern with a clear condition and possible consequence; distinguish a precise objection from vague politeness or an unsupported universal claim.

sections.title: Compare Options Against the Same Criteria
sections.learningOutcome: Compare two concrete proposals using the same task-relevant criteria, while separating possible advantages from unverified outcomes.

sections.title: Revise a Proposal Without Inventing Agreement
sections.learningOutcome: Revise a proposal in response to a specific concern and record only the agreement actually expressed, leaving unanswered questions visible.

sections.title: Rehearse a Constructive Disagreement
sections.learningOutcome: Privately rehearse a clear, respectful disagreement that addresses the actual proposal, explains a relevant concern and leaves the group a concrete question or alternative to examine.

sections.title: Transfer and Review
sections.learningOutcome: Express a task-relevant disagreement in a new setting, propose a way to examine it, and distinguish procedural agreement from agreement on the final choice.
